stories.hook: Borrowing costs keep climbing: the 10-year is at 5.24%
stories.what: The 10-year Treasury yield ended Oct. 9 at 5.24%, up from 4.79% on Sept. 1.
stories.why: It's the benchmark for mortgages and corporate bonds, so borrowing gets pricier.
stories.ib: It's the usual risk-free rate in a DCF: higher yield, higher cost of equity and WACC, lower valuations.
stories.ctx: With yields above 5%, debt-funded deals get harder: interest eats into EPS accretion and LBO returns.

stories.hook: Paramount completes its Warner Bros. Discovery takeover
stories.what: Paramount closed its cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery at just over $31 a share. The combined company is now called Skydance.
stories.why: Closing makes it a done deal: debt is drawn, target shares are cancelled, integration begins.
stories.ib: Funded with $47 billion of new equity plus bank and Apollo-led debt: a textbook sources-and-uses table.
stories.ctx: Mega-mergers can take months to close; this one needed sign-off from competition authorities in nearly 70 jurisdictions.
stories.hist: A modern media mega-merger and a reference point for how very large deals are financed with a mix of new equity and debt.

stories.hook: C.H. Robinson agrees to buy RXO for $5.8 billion
stories.what: RXO holders get $17.25 in cash plus 0.0856 C.H. Robinson shares each, about $30.25 a share in total.
stories.uncertain: Needs regulatory and shareholder approval; expected in the first half of 2027.
stories.why: Paying partly in stock means less borrowing, and RXO holders share in the combined company.
stories.ib: Bankers model the new debt's interest and the extra shares when testing accretion/dilution.
stories.ctx: Stock-and-cash deals are a middle path: less new debt for the buyer, and the target's holders share any synergies.

stories.hook: Schneider Electric bids $205 a share in cash for PTC
stories.what: Schneider Electric agreed to buy software maker PTC for $205 a share in cash, about $22.6 billion of equity, a 42.3% premium.
stories.uncertain: Needs shareholder and regulatory approval; closing expected by Q3 2027.
stories.why: That premium means Schneider expects synergies the market wasn't pricing in.
stories.ib: It's funded mostly with €16–17 billion of new debt, so accretion hinges on interest cost versus PTC's earnings.
stories.ctx: Industrial companies keep buying software: recurring revenue supports high premiums and lots of acquisition debt.

stories.hook: Hiring nearly stalls: 29,000 jobs added in September
stories.what: Payrolls rose 29,000 and unemployment held at 4.2%. July was revised to a loss of 10,000 jobs.
stories.why: Slow hiring plus elevated inflation pulls the Fed two ways, so each report moves rate expectations.
stories.ib: Expected rates set the risk-free rate in a DCF and the cost of LBO debt.
stories.ctx: Weak hiring right after a rate hike is an awkward mix for the Fed, and it shapes what deal financing costs.

stories.hook: Micron's quarterly revenue jumps nearly fivefold on AI demand
stories.what: Micron reported quarterly revenue of $54.23 billion, up from $11.32 billion a year earlier, and guided to about $61.5 billion next quarter.
stories.why: Memory chips feed AI data centers, so this shows AI spending reaching suppliers.
stories.ib: Growth this fast makes trailing multiples look cheap, so bankers lean on forward estimates.
stories.ctx: Memory chips are famously cyclical: booms have often been followed by price drops, so analysts argue over normalized earnings.

stories.hook: A private-equity-backed IPO prices at $18 a share
stories.what: Accelevation priced 30 million shares at $18.00 on Nasdaq (ACCV). Two-thirds were sold by holders affiliated with Olympus Partners.
stories.why: Most shares came from the owners, not the company: a PE firm starting to cash out.
stories.ib: An IPO is a PE exit route: selling in stages locks in returns while keeping some upside.
stories.ctx: Bankers watch PE-backed listings: when funds can exit through IPOs, they return cash and raise money for new deals.

stories.hook: Priority Technology's CEO leads a $1.6 billion buyout
stories.what: A group led by CEO Thomas Priore will buy the payments firm for $8.05 a share: a $1.6 billion enterprise value.
stories.uncertain: Needs unaffiliated holders' approval; expected in the first half of 2027.
stories.why: Insiders buying out public holders have to show the price is fair.
stories.ib: Backed by Searchlight Capital equity, it's a management buyout: returns hinge on debt paydown and the exit.
stories.ctx: Management buyouts show the LBO toolkit in miniature: borrowed money, a premium for public holders, a plan to sell later.

stories.hook: The Fed raises rates a quarter point to fight inflation
stories.what: The Fed voted 12–0 on Sept. 16 to raise rates 1/4 point, to 3.75%–4.00%, citing elevated inflation.
stories.why: Costlier borrowing lowers what investors will pay today for future profits.
stories.ib: Rates feed the risk-free rate and the cost of debt: WACC rises, DCF values fall, LBOs carry less debt.
stories.ctx: Hiking while inflation runs hot is classic tightening: discount rates rise in every valuation.
stories.hist: A reminder that rates can rise as well as fall: every DCF, LBO and merger model leans on what money costs.

updates.text: Minutes out Oct. 7: most officials see another hike as likely by year end.
